Tailcat connection

Source: R/connection.R
TailcatConnection.Rd

A TCP stream or connected UDP flow between a TailcatClient and a TailcatServer. Connections are created by TailcatClient$dial() and TailcatListener$accept(), not directly.

For TCP, reads may return fewer bytes than requested and $read() returns NULL at end of stream. For UDP, each read returns one datagram (possibly raw(0)) and each write sends one datagram of at most 1232 bytes.

One read and one write may be in flight at the same time (for example a pending $read_async() while writing). Further operations in the same direction wait their turn and run in the order they were started, for synchronous and asynchronous calls alike, so several $write_async() calls send their data in call order and several $read_async() calls receive consecutive chunks of the stream in call order. The wait counts toward each operation's timeout, and canceling or timing out an operation that is still waiting ends it without affecting the others.

$client or $server (the other is NULL) gives the object that owns the connection, the client that dialed it or the server whose listener accepted it.

Once the connection, or the client or server that owns it, is closed, every method other than $close(), $format(), and $print(), and every field other than $is_closed, $client, and $server, raises a tailcat_closed error; nothing is kept from before. Timeouts (including timeout = 0, a poll) and errors are described in TailcatServer.

Because of an upstream tailcat bug, $info() (and so $local_address and $remote_address) fails with tailcat_failure, and the Go runtime prints a stack trace to standard error, on a TCP connection whose two directions have both been shut down (both sides called $close_write()). $print() and $format() avoid this by leaving the endpoints out once $close_write() has succeeded on the connection.

Active bindings

local_address

The local endpoint as "host:port" on the tailcat network. It is fetched from tailcat on each access.

remote_address

The peer's endpoint as "host:port" on the tailcat network. It is fetched from tailcat on each access.

network

"tcp" or "udp".

client

The TailcatClient that dialed the connection, or NULL for an accepted connection. Like $server, it keeps working after the connection is closed.

server

The TailcatServer whose listener accepted the connection, or NULL for a dialed connection. It keeps working after the connection is closed.

is_closed

TRUE once the connection, or the client or server that owns it, has been closed.

TailcatConnection$read()

Read up to n bytes (TCP) or one datagram (UDP, truncated to n bytes). One call returns at most 65536 bytes whatever the value of n (TCP reads may return less than requested anyway, and UDP datagrams are much smaller), so loop, or use $read_all(), to read more. A timeout ends only this read; the connection stays usable. With timeout = 0 the read returns data (or the end of stream) that has already arrived, and otherwise raises tailcat_timeout at once. A TCP read returns whatever has arrived, so with as = "text" a multibyte UTF-8 character can be split across two reads; for multibyte text use $read_all(), or read raw bytes and convert them once. On UDP, n = 0 is not supported: because of an upstream tailcat bug it fails and the datagram is lost.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read(n = 65536L, timeout = Inf, as = c("raw", "text"))

Arguments

n

Maximum number of bytes to return (at most 65536 are returned).

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

as

Exactly "raw" (the default) to return a raw vector, or "text" to return a single string marked as UTF-8 (the bytes are not checked for valid UTF-8). Data containing NUL bytes cannot be returned as text and raises a tailcat_invalid_argument error; the data is consumed, so read binary data with as = "raw".

Returns

A raw vector or a string, or NULL at TCP end of stream.

TailcatConnection$read_async()

Asynchronous version of $read().

Usage

TailcatConnection$read_async(n = 65536L, timeout = Inf, as = c("raw", "text"))

Arguments

n

Maximum number of bytes to return.

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

as

"raw" or "text", as for $read().

Returns

A promise resolving with a raw vector or a string, or NULL at TCP end of stream.

TailcatConnection$read_all()

Read until the peer ends the stream (TCP only). On timeout or error the condition's bytes field gives the number of bytes read before it; those bytes are discarded. With timeout = 0 it returns only if the whole stream, including its end, has already arrived.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read_all(
  timeout = Inf,
  as = c("raw", "text"),
  max_bytes = Inf
)

Arguments

timeout

Overall seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

as

Exactly "raw" (the default) to return a raw vector, or "text" to return a single string marked as UTF-8 ("" for an empty stream). See $read() for NUL bytes.

max_bytes

The most bytes to accept, a single non-negative whole number or Inf (the default) for no limit. If the stream is longer, reading stops after max_bytes + 1 bytes and a tailcat_failure error is raised whose bytes field is the number of bytes read (max_bytes + 1). Those bytes are discarded, but the connection stays open and usable: the rest of the stream can still be read, or the connection closed.

Returns

A raw vector or a string.

TailcatConnection$read_all_async()

Asynchronous version of $read_all(). Canceling the promise with tailcat_cancel() ends the read in flight and starts no further reads.

Usage

TailcatConnection$read_all_async(
  timeout = Inf,
  as = c("raw", "text"),
  max_bytes = Inf
)

Arguments

timeout

Overall seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

as

"raw" or "text", as for $read_all().

max_bytes

The most bytes to accept, as for $read_all(); a longer stream rejects the promise with a tailcat_failure error.

Returns

A promise resolving with a raw vector or a string.

TailcatConnection$write()

Write all of data. On timeout or error the condition's bytes field gives the number of bytes already sent.

Usage

TailcatConnection$write(data, timeout = Inf)

Arguments

data

A raw vector, or a character vector which is pasted together without separators and sent as UTF-8.

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls (sends what can be sent at once).

Returns

The number of bytes written (an integer, or a double beyond the integer range), invisibly.

TailcatConnection$close_write()

Half-close a TCP connection: tell the peer there is nothing more to send, while still being able to read its reply.

Usage

Arguments

timeout

Seconds to wait for pending writes; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

Returns

The connection, invisibly.

Asynchronous version of $close_write().

Usage

TailcatConnection$close_write_async(timeout = 30)

Arguments

timeout

Seconds to wait; Inf waits indefinitely and 0 polls.

Returns

A promise resolving with the connection.

TailcatConnection$readable()

Check without waiting whether a TCP read would return immediately (buffered data, end of stream, or a pending error). Intended for checking idle connections, not as a readiness loop.

Usage

TailcatConnection$readable()

Returns

TRUE or FALSE.

TailcatConnection$close()

Close the connection. Pending reads and writes end with a tailcat_closed error. Closing twice is harmless.

Usage

TailcatConnection$close()

Returns

The connection, invisibly.

TailcatConnection$format()

Format a summary, the lines that $print() shows. An open connection shows its local and remote endpoints on the tailcat network (not secrets); they are left out when the connection is closed, when tailcat cannot report them, and once $close_write() has succeeded on it, because asking tailcat after both sides have shut down their writes triggers an upstream bug that prints a Go stack trace.

Usage

TailcatConnection$format(...)

Arguments

...

Ignored.

Returns

A character vector.

TailcatConnection$print()

Print the summary from $format().

Usage

TailcatConnection$print(...)

Arguments

...

Ignored.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn = TailcatClient$new(address)$dial(8080)
conn$write("ping")
conn$close_write()
conn$read_all(timeout = 10, as = "text")
} # }
